First off, this hit home for me pretty hard, in a melancholy but good way. I'm dealing with the grief from losing my little brother. July 20th marks the anniversary of his passing two years ago. He passed away in a drowning accident less than a month after getting married. Time seemed to stop after he passed for most of my family.

I'm no expert when it comes to imagery in movies. However, for me, watching the beginning it seemed like he was contemplating ways of ending his life, but was always stopping himself short because he was either too depressed to go all the way through with it, or there were other things tying him to life still.

Him leaving the house to go outside seemed to me that it showed he was making an effort to move on but the pieces of his loved one still fell down around him reminding him of his child. For me, and what I've seen in my family we all make an effort to move forward in life but are always reminded of him in both sad and happy ways in a mix of emotions.

The biggest part that struck a cord with me was while I deal with my grief in a different way, I see this film parallel a lot of what I've seen my dad go through to an extent. Not caring anymore about his own life yet staying around for the rest of us. I think this is because, well, we're still here...

Thank you for sharing this.

Wow. I don't even know what to say. I don't think I've ever heard that one of our films affected someone. I am deeply sorry for your loss. Your comment brought some tears to my eyes. Hang in there, and if you ever need to talk to a random person with no biases towards your situation you can certainly talk to me.

Sound quality was very good all the lines were relatively crisp and clear and the music was something special.

The acting was a bit forced on both ends. Both of you seemed like you knew what you wanted to do too well, what I mean by that is there wasn't a sense of discovery by the characters as the story progressed. Little things can help, like when the girl picks up the bottles on the floor and says they're still half full even just pausing for a second and giving the bottle a shake to discover for herself that they are in fact half full can make the sense of discovery a bit more alive. Both actors seemed to find places of comfort which is dangerous because comfort to them comes across as laziness to the audience and I felt that both actors found their marks and stopped on them.

As for cinematography, there were quite a few really impressive shots and some beautiful scenes. Overall it felt a bit plain. Putting something or someone in the spotlight makes them pop and I like pop, but that's more personal preference than anything. Throw in some shadows though, it never hurts.
